proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a law \(P\in\mathcal M\).  All conditional moments below exist by \(\texttt{ass:moment-radius}\), and conditioning on every cohort is legitimate because \(p_c\geq p_\star>0\) by \(\texttt{ass:positive-shares}\).  From \(\texttt{ass:rank-two-factor-law}\) and \(\texttt{ass:error-mean}\),
\[
 \nu_c
 =\mathbb E_P[J_cY_i(0)\mid C_i=c]
 =\Gamma_{S_c}\mathbb E_P[\lambda_i\mid C_i=c]
 =\Gamma_{S_c}m_c.                                      \tag{1}
\]
Using also \(\texttt{ass:loading-error-orthogonality}\) and \(\texttt{ass:conditional-homoskedasticity}\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 V_c
 &=\operatorname{Cov}_P(\Gamma_{S_c}\lambda_i+\varepsilon_{i,S_c}\mid C_i=c)\\
 &=\Gamma_{S_c}H_c\Gamma_{S_c}^{\prime}+\sigma_c^2I_{|S_c|}.
 \end{aligned}                                                            \tag{2}
\]
The signal term in (2) has rank two and second eigenvalue at least \(g_\star>0\) by \(\texttt{ass:local-signal-gap}\).  Hence the two largest eigenvalues of \(V_c\) are strictly larger than its remaining eigenvalues, all of which equal \(\sigma_c^2\), and therefore
\[
 \Pi_2(V_c)=\Pi_{\operatorname{col}(\Gamma_{S_c})},
 \qquad
 Q_c=I_{|S_c|}-\Pi_{\operatorname{col}(\Gamma_{S_c})}.                  \tag{3}
\]
Thus \(p_c\), \(\nu_c\), \(V_c\), and \(Q_c\) are functionals of the complete observed law \(P_O\), rather than latent-model definitions.

Let \(\mathcal L=\operatorname{col}(\Gamma)\).  Since \(B_c^{\prime}B_c=Q_c\), \(B_cB_c^{\prime}=I\), and \(p_c>0\), the relation construction \(\texttt{def:relation-operator}\) and (3) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \ker\overline R(P)
 &=\bigcap_{c=1}^C\ker(B_cJ_c)\\
 &=\{x\in\mathbb R^T:Q_cx_{S_c}=0\text{ for every }c\}\\
 &=\{x\in\mathbb R^T:x_{S_c}\in\operatorname{col}(\Gamma_{S_c})
                     \text{ for every }c\}.
 \end{aligned}                                                            \tag{4}
\]
In particular, \(\mathcal L\subseteq\ker\overline R(P)\).

The cited coordinate-projection certificate \(\texttt{lem:generic-rank-two-coordinate-projection-certificate}\), applied with rank two and with the anchor expansion in \(\texttt{def:anchor-hypergraph}\), says that on the generic locus selected by \(\texttt{ass:generic-factor-rows}\), the local planes \(\operatorname{col}(\Gamma_{S_c})\) determine \(\mathcal L\) uniquely exactly when there is a set \(F\) of \(T-2\) anchor triples satisfying
\[
 |F'|\leq |V(F')|-2\qquad\text{for every nonempty }F'\subseteq F.       \tag{5}
\]
By \(\texttt{def:pebble-certificate}\), condition (5) is exactly \(r_{1,2}(H_3)=T-2\); a set of \(T-2\) triples satisfying (5) necessarily has vertex union \([T]\), because applying (5) to \(F\) yields \(T-2\leq |V(F)|-2\leq T-2\).

We next connect uniqueness in that cited result to the linear kernel in (4).  If \(\ker\overline R(P)=\mathcal L\), uniqueness is immediate.  Conversely, suppose the local planes uniquely determine \(\mathcal L\) but \(\dim\ker\overline R(P)>2\).  Choose \(h\in\ker\overline R(P)\setminus\mathcal L\) and a basis \(u_1,u_2\) of \(\mathcal L\).  For all sufficiently small nonzero \(z\),
\[
 \mathcal L_z=\operatorname{span}(u_1+zh,u_2)                             \tag{6}
\]
is different from \(\mathcal L\).  Equation (4) gives \((\mathcal L_z)_{S_c}\subseteq\operatorname{col}(\Gamma_{S_c})\).  At \(z=0\) every restricted plane has rank two by \(\texttt{ass:local-signal-gap}\); since there are finitely many cohorts, continuity of one nonzero two-by-two minor for each cohort shows that all these restrictions still have rank two for sufficiently small \(|z|\).  Their inclusion is then equality, contradicting uniqueness.  Consequently,
\[
 r_{1,2}(H_3)=T-2
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \ker\overline R(P)=\operatorname{col}(\Gamma).                         \tag{7}
\]

Assume first that the certificate passes.  Let \(U\) be any orthonormal basis of the observed-law kernel in (7).  The normalization \(\Gamma^{\prime}\Gamma=I_2\) from \(\texttt{ass:factor-normalization}\) implies that \(U=\Gamma W\) for an orthogonal two-by-two matrix \(W\).  Moreover, \(U_{S_c}\) has full column rank by the local signal gap, so division by \(U_{S_c}^{\prime}U_{S_c}\) is valid.  Substituting (1) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 U(U_{S_c}^{\prime}U_{S_c})^{-1}U_{S_c}^{\prime}\nu_c
 &=U(U_{S_c}^{\prime}U_{S_c})^{-1}U_{S_c}^{\prime}\Gamma_{S_c}m_c\\
 &=U W^{\prime}m_c
 =\Gamma m_c
 =\mu_c(P).
 \end{aligned}                                                            \tag{8}
\]
Replacing \(U\) by \(UW_0\) for any orthogonal \(W_0\) leaves the first expression in (8) unchanged, so (8) is basis independent.  It is precisely \(\texttt{def:counterfactual-functional}\), assembled only from \(P_O\).  Thus if two laws in \(\mathcal M\) have the same observed law, they have the same quantities on the left of (8) and hence the same entire causal target \(\mu\).  This proves model-wide identification rather than defining the causal target to equal an observed regression quantity.

For the converse, assume \(r_{1,2}(H_3)<T-2\) and take the perturbably interior law \(P^\circ\) in the narrowed statement.  Write its factor matrix, loadings, and errors as \(\Gamma\), \(\lambda_i\), and \(\varepsilon_i\), and put \(\mathcal K=\ker\overline R(P^\circ)\).  By (7), \(\dim\mathcal K>2\), while \(\mathcal L\subseteq\mathcal K\).  Hence there is a unit vector
\[
 h\in\mathcal K\cap\mathcal L^\perp.                                   \tag{9}
\]
For every cohort, (4) and full column rank of \(\Gamma_{S_c}\) yield the unique vector
\[
 b_c=\Gamma_{S_c}^{\dagger}h_{S_c},
 \qquad h_{S_c}=\Gamma_{S_c}b_c.                                         \tag{10}
\]
Let \(a=m_{c_0}^\circ\neq0\).  For a scalar \(d\), define
\[
 L_c(d)=I_2+d b_ca^{\prime},
 \qquad
 \widetilde\Gamma_d=\Gamma+d h a^{\prime}.                              \tag{11}
\]
Because \(C\) is finite, the matrix-determinant identity
\[
 \det L_c(d)=1+d a^{\prime}b_c                                           \tag{12}
\]
shows that every \(L_c(d)\) is invertible for all sufficiently small \(|d|\).  Equations (10)--(11) give the exact, cohort-specific factor identity
\[
 (\widetilde\Gamma_d)_{S_c}
 =\Gamma_{S_c}+d h_{S_c}a^{\prime}
 =\Gamma_{S_c}L_c(d).                                                     \tag{13}
\]
For small \(|d|\), \(\widetilde\Gamma_d\) has rank two.  Define
\[
 G_d=(\widetilde\Gamma_d^{\prime}\widetilde\Gamma_d)^{-1/2},
 \qquad
 \Gamma_d=\widetilde\Gamma_dG_d,
 \qquad
 \lambda_{i,d}=G_d^{-1}L_c(d)^{-1}\lambda_i
 \quad\text{when }C_i=c,                                                 \tag{14}
\]
and retain \(\varepsilon_{i,d}=\varepsilon_i\).  The inverse square root in (14) exists by rank two, and
\[
 \Gamma_d^{\prime}\Gamma_d
 =G_d\widetilde\Gamma_d^{\prime}\widetilde\Gamma_dG_d
 =I_2.                                                                    \tag{15}
\]
On a common probability space keep \(C_i\), \(\lambda_i\), and \(\varepsilon_i\) from \(P^\circ\), and use (14) to define a new full-data law \(P_d\).  For a unit in cohort \(c\), equations (13)--(14) imply the pathwise identity
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 (\Gamma_d\lambda_{i,d}+\varepsilon_{i,d})_{S_c}
 &=\widetilde\Gamma_{d,S_c}G_dG_d^{-1}L_c(d)^{-1}\lambda_i
   +\varepsilon_{i,S_c}\\
 &=\Gamma_{S_c}L_c(d)L_c(d)^{-1}\lambda_i+\varepsilon_{i,S_c}\\
 &=\Gamma_{S_c}\lambda_i+\varepsilon_{i,S_c}.
 \end{aligned}                                                            \tag{16}
\]
Thus (16) equates the whole observed random vector, not merely its mean and covariance.  Keeping the cohort draw and taking independent copies therefore yields
\[
 (P_d)_O=(P^\circ)_O.                                                     \tag{17}
\]

It remains to verify that this is a legal deformation rather than a latent reparametrization outside the class.  Conditional loading means and covariances under \(P_d\) are
\[
 m_{c,d}=G_d^{-1}L_c(d)^{-1}m_c^\circ,
 \qquad
 H_{c,d}=G_d^{-1}L_c(d)^{-1}H_c^\circ L_c(d)^{-\prime}G_d^{-\prime}.      \tag{18}
\]
The maps in (18) converge to \(m_c^\circ\) and \(H_c^\circ\) as \(d\to0\).  The strict covariance inequalities in the narrowed statement and continuity of eigenvalues therefore imply
\[
 v_\star I_2\preceq H_{c,d}\preceq v^\star I_2                         \tag{19}
\]
for every cohort and all sufficiently small \(|d|\).  More strongly, (13), (14), and (18) give
\[
 \Gamma_{d,S_c}H_{c,d}\Gamma_{d,S_c}^{\prime}
 =\Gamma_{S_c}H_c^\circ\Gamma_{S_c}^{\prime},                           \tag{20}
\]
so the local signal eigengap is preserved exactly, including when its lower bound is attained.  Since the linear maps in (14) converge to the identity and the conditional moment inequalities at \(P^\circ\) are strict,
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_d}\!\left[\|\lambda_{i,d}\|^{4+\delta}
       +\|\varepsilon_{i,d}\|^{4+\delta}\mid C_i=c\right]
 \leq M_{\mathrm{mom}}                                                   \tag{21}
\]
for every cohort after reducing \(|d|\) if necessary.  Conditional error means and covariances are unchanged, and
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_{P_d}(\lambda_{i,d},\varepsilon_{i,d}\mid C_i=c)
 =G_d^{-1}L_c(d)^{-1}
   \operatorname{Cov}_{P^\circ}(\lambda_i,\varepsilon_i\mid C_i=c)
 =0.                                                                      \tag{22}
\]
Cohort shares and deterministic masks are unchanged.  Rank and normalization follow from (14)--(15).  The local projected planes in (13) are unchanged; equivalently, their relation rows are unchanged up to invertible within-cohort transformations.  Hence the relation-matroid genericity in \(\texttt{ass:generic-factor-rows}\) is preserved; alternatively, the complement of the algebraic exceptional set is open at \(d=0\), so the same conclusion holds after reducing \(|d|\).  Equations (19)--(22), together with the unchanged assumptions, prove \(P_d\in\mathcal M\).  The transformed conditional loading distribution itself witnesses \((m_{c,d})_{c=1}^C\in\mathfrak M_\lambda(H_d)\) under \(\texttt{def:admissible-loading-means}\).

Finally, the Sherman--Morrison identity and (11) yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mu_c(P_d)-\mu_c(P^\circ)
 &=\widetilde\Gamma_dL_c(d)^{-1}m_c^\circ-\Gamma m_c^\circ\\
 &=\frac{d}{1+d a^{\prime}b_c}
      (h-\Gamma b_c)(a^{\prime}m_c^\circ).
 \end{aligned}                                                            \tag{23}
\]
At \(c=c_0\), \(a^{\prime}m_{c_0}^\circ=\|m_{c_0}^\circ\|^2>0\).  Moreover, (9), \(\Gamma^{\prime}\Gamma=I_2\), and (10) imply
\[
 \|h-\Gamma b_{c_0}\|^2
 =\|h\|^2+\|b_{c_0}\|^2>0,
 \qquad
 (h-\Gamma b_{c_0})_{S_{c_0}}=0.                                        \tag{24}
\]
Therefore the nonzero vector in (24) has at least one nonzero coordinate outside \(S_{c_0}\).  For any sufficiently small nonzero \(d\), (23) changes that missing cohort-time mean.  Taking \(P_0=P^\circ\) and \(P_1=P_d\), equations (17) and (23)--(24) give
\[
 P_{0,O}=P_{1,O},
 \qquad
 \mu(P_0)\neq\mu(P_1).                                                   \tag{25}
\]
No functional of the entire observed law can take two different values on the same law, so (25) proves failure of model-wide identification.  Together with (8), this establishes both directions of the narrowed theorem.

added_lemmas.statement: Let \(S=(S_c)_{c=1}^C\) have \(|S_c|\geq 3\), and expand every support \(S_c\) into the anchor triples of \(H_3\).  For almost every two-dimensional subspace of \(\mathbb R^T\), its coordinate projections on the supports \(S_c\) determine it uniquely if and only if the expanded triple multiset contains \(T-2\) triples such that every subcollection of \(k\) triples is supported on at least \(k+2\) coordinates.

For generic factor rows, over all laws \(P\in\mathcal M\) whose cohort loading-mean vector ranges over \(\mathfrak M_{\lambda}(H)\), every coordinate of \(\mu(P)\) is a functional of the entire observed law \(P_O\) if and only if \(r_{1,2}(H_3)=T-2\). proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen converse is false without a feasibility condition: the displayed primitive restrictions permit \(p_{\star}>1/C\), making \(\mathcal M\) empty, and binding covariance or moment radii can also eliminate every nonzero admissible loading mean or every perturbation neighborhood. The added condition requires only a nonzero-mean interior witness for the legal full-law transport; it does not assume observational equivalence, target separation, or the theorem's crux.

proofs.proof_tex:
For the first implication, apply \(\operatorname{lem:lei-ross-o3-nullspace}\) to a generic two-plane. It gives \(\ker A=\operatorname{col}(\Gamma)\), so \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=T-2\). The cited theorem uses equal positive cohort weights, but the kernel is unchanged by the core's positive weights because
\[
x'A(P)x=\sum_cp_c\|Q_cJ_cx\|^2=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
Q_cJ_cx=0\quad\text{for every }c.
\]
Within cohort \(c\), the \(|S_c|-2\) anchor-triple relations span the orthogonal complement of \(\operatorname{col}(\Gamma_{S_c})\): each nonanchor coordinate appears in exactly one anchor relation with a nonzero coefficient, because a generic anchor pair is linearly independent. Thus their padded global row span equals the row span defining \(A\). The generic independence criterion in \(\operatorname{lem:generic-three-coordinate-relation-independence}\) identifies its rank with \(r_{1,2}(H_3)\). Hence \(r_{1,2}(H_3)=T-2\).

For the four masks, the four anchor triples are
\[
123,\qquad145,\qquad256,\qquad346.
\]
Every pair intersects in one vertex, every three cover all six vertices, and all four cover six vertices. Therefore a subfamily of size \(k=1,2,3,4\) has respectively at least \(3,4,5,6=k+2\) vertices. The four-edge family is \((1,2)\)-sparse and tight, so \(r_{1,2}(H_3)=4\). On the other hand, every pair of masks intersects in only one outcome. The rank-two \(O_3\) graph therefore has no edge at its first iteration and terminates without a merge.

Let \(X\) have rows \((1,t)\), \(t=1,\ldots,6\). Direct row multiplication gives
\[
DX=0.
\]
The determinant of the first four columns of \(D\) is \(-11\); hence its four rows are independent and \(\operatorname{rank}(D)=4\). For equal shares, an orthonormal-row relation matrix is
\[
R=\frac12\operatorname{diag}(6^{-1/2},26^{-1/2},26^{-1/2},14^{-1/2})D.
\]
Writing \(x\) for an eigenvalue of \(R'R\), exact determinant expansion gives
\[
\det(xI-R'R)=\frac{x^2}{4845568}f(x),
\quad
f(x)=4845568x^4-4845568x^3+1601152x^2-189696x+4235. \tag{1}
\]
On \([0,3/100]\), the derivative of \(f/4845568\) is at most
\[
4(3/100)^3+\frac{1787}{2704}(3/100)-\frac{57}{1456}
=-\frac{22730361}{1183000000}<0. \tag{2}
\]
For \(a=16936528/10^8\) and \(b=16936530/10^8\), clearing positive denominators yields
\[
f(a^2)=\frac{161278657620904604391277014466117463622902567103}{568434188608080148696899414062500000000000000000000}>0,
\]
and
\[
f(b^2)=-\frac{11157943628704037946208225251724738321835808755137}{24414062500000000000000000000000000000000000000000000}<0.
\]
Because \(R'R\) is positive semidefinite, (1)--(2) show that its smallest positive eigenvalue lies strictly between \(a^2\) and \(b^2\). Thus \(a<s<b\).

Finally put \(z=19/5+\eta\). Relations for the two masks containing coordinate six change to
\[
D_3(z)=(0,5-z,0,0,z-2,-3),\qquad
D_4(z)=(0,0,4-z,z-3,0,-1).
\]
Every four-by-four minor of \(D(z)\) contains the factor \(5z-19\), while, for example, the minor on columns \(1,2,3,6\) equals \(19-5z=-5\eta\). At \(z=19/5\), the first three rows and first three columns have determinant \(6/5\), so \(\operatorname{rank}D(19/5)=3\). After continuous positive row normalization and the factor \(1/2\) from equal shares, call the result \(R(z)\). Weyl's elementary variational inequality gives
\[
\sigma_4\{R(z)\}\leq\|R(z)-R(19/5)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq C|\eta|. \tag{3}
\]
Cauchy--Binet and the displayed nonzero minor give
\[
\prod_{j=1}^4\sigma_j\{R(z)\}=\det\{R(z)R(z)'\}^{1/2}\geq c|\eta|. \tag{4}
\]
The first three singular values are uniformly bounded above near \(\eta=0\), so (4) implies \(\sigma_4\{R(z)\}\geq c'|\eta|\). Equations (3)--(4) prove \(s(P_\eta)\asymp|\eta|\). In each mask the three slopes remain distinct for sufficiently small \(|\eta|\); hence its three-by-two factor restriction has rank two. Right multiplication by the invertible orthonormalizing matrix changes neither this rank nor any relation projector.

Put \(q_0=4+\delta\). Since \(\|\Gamma\|_{\mathrm{op}}=1\), the conditional moment bound and \((x+y)^4\leq8(x^4+y^4)\) imply a uniform fourth-moment bound
\[
\max_c\mathbb E_P[\|J_cY_i(0)\|^4\mid C_i=c]\leq K. \tag{1}
\]
Also Jensen's inequality gives \(\|m_c\|\leq B\), hence \(|\mu_{ct}|\leq B\); clipping cannot increase coordinatewise error relative to \(\mu\).

Let \(N_c=\sum_i1\{C_i=c\}\), and let \(G_N=\{N_c\geq Np_\star/2\text{ for all }c\}\). Chebyshev's inequality and \(\operatorname{Var}(N_c)\leq N\) give \(\Pr_P(G_N^c)\leq K/N\), after increasing \(K\) to cover finitely many small \(N\). Conditional on the counts and on \(G_N\), elementary sample-mean and sample-covariance calculations using (1) give
\[
\mathbb E_P\!\left[\sum_c\{\|\widehat\nu_c-\nu_c\|^2+\|\widehat V_c-V_c\|_{\mathrm F}^2\}+\|\widehat p-p\|^2;G_N\right]\leq\frac K N. \tag{2}
\]

Let \(P_c=I-Q_c\) and \(\widehat P_c=I-\widehat Q_c\). The local eigenvalue gap is at least \(g_\star\). The variational trace argument in equations (2) of \(\operatorname{lem:observed-moment-inverse-modulus}\), applied to \(V_c\) and \(\widehat V_c\), yields
\[
\|\widehat Q_c-Q_c\|_{\mathrm F}\leq K\|\widehat V_c-V_c\|_{\mathrm F}. \tag{3}
\]
Define padded relation matrices
\[
\mathcal R=\operatorname{stack}_c\sqrt{p_c}\,Q_cJ_c,
\qquad
\widehat{\mathcal R}=\operatorname{stack}_c\sqrt{\widehat p_c}\,\widehat Q_cJ_c.
\]
They have Gram matrices \(A\) and \(\widehat A\), so \(\widehat U\) consists of the bottom two right singular vectors of \(\widehat{\mathcal R}\). On \(G_N\), (2)--(3) and the share floor imply
\[
\mathbb E_P[\|\widehat{\mathcal R}-\mathcal R\|_{\mathrm F}^2;G_N]\leq K/N. \tag{4}
\]

Let \(U\) be an orthonormal basis of \(\ker\mathcal R=\operatorname{col}(\Gamma)\). Variational optimality of \(\widehat U\), using \(U\) as a competitor, gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|\mathcal R\widehat U\|_{\mathrm F}
&\leq\|(\mathcal R-\widehat{\mathcal R})\widehat U\|_{\mathrm F}+\|\widehat{\mathcal R}\widehat U\|_{\mathrm F}\\
&\leq\sqrt2\|\mathcal R-\widehat{\mathcal R}\|_{\mathrm F}+\|\widehat{\mathcal R}U\|_{\mathrm F}\\
&\leq2\sqrt2\|\widehat{\mathcal R}-\mathcal R\|_{\mathrm F}.
\end{aligned} \tag{5}
\]
Since \(s(P)\geq s_N\), restriction of \(\mathcal R\) to \(\operatorname{col}(U)^\perp\) has smallest singular value at least \(s_N\). Therefore
\[
\|(I-UU')\widehat U\|_{\mathrm F}
\leq \frac{2\sqrt2}{s_N}\|\widehat{\mathcal R}-\mathcal R\|_{\mathrm F}. \tag{6}
\]
The local conditioning bound (5) in \(\operatorname{lem:observed-moment-inverse-modulus}\) supplies \(a=\sqrt{g_\star/v^\star}>0\). Whenever the left side of (6) is at most a fixed sufficiently small multiple of \(a\), orthogonal alignment, the inverse identity \(G^{-1}-\widehat G^{-1}=G^{-1}(\widehat G-G)\widehat G^{-1}\), and the true equality \(\nu_c=\Gamma_{S_c}m_c\) give
\[
\|\widehat\mu-\mu\|_\infty
\leq K\left\{\max_c\|\widehat\nu_c-\nu_c\|+\frac{\|\widehat{\mathcal R}-\mathcal R\|_{\mathrm F}}{s_N}\right\}. \tag{7}
\]
On the complementary event, or on the corrected fallback branch, the truncated loss is at most one. Markov's inequality applied to (4) bounds the probability of failure of the smallness condition by \(K/(Ns_N^2)\). Squaring (7), applying (2) and (4), and adding \(\Pr(G_N^c)\leq K/N\leq K/(Ns_N^2)\), gives
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}\mathbb E_PL(\widehat\mu,\mu(P))\leq\frac K{Ns_N^2}.
\]
The loss is at most one, so taking the smaller of this bound and one proves the claim.

Put \(q_0=4+\delta\). For every coordinate \(X=Z_{ij}\), the factor normalization and the conditional moment restriction imply
\[
\operatorname{Var}_P(X)\leq\mathbb E_PX^2\leq \Sigma^2,
\qquad
\Sigma\leq K\{1+M_{\mathrm{mom}}^{2/q_0}\}. \tag{1}
\]
Indeed probability coordinates are bounded, first-moment coordinates satisfy \(Y_t^2\leq\|\lambda\|^2+2\|\lambda\|\|\varepsilon\|+\|\varepsilon\|^2\), and for a second-moment coordinate \((Y_tY_u)^2\leq\|Y\|^4\leq8(\|\lambda\|^4+\|\varepsilon\|^4)\); Lyapunov's inequality then gives (1).

Let \(k=k_\alpha\), and let \(n_b\) be a block size. When \(N\geq2k\), \(n_b\geq N/(2k)\). For a block mean \(\overline X_b\), Chebyshev's inequality gives
\[
\Pr_P\{|\overline X_b-\mathbb EX|>4\Sigma\sqrt{k/N}\}\leq\frac18. \tag{2}
\]
The blocks are independent. If their median violates the same inequality, at least \(\lceil k/2\rceil\) block means violate it. Consequently
\[
\Pr_P\{|\widehat\theta_j-\theta_j|>4\Sigma\sqrt{k/N}\}
\leq \binom{k}{\lceil k/2\rceil}2^{-3\lceil k/2\rceil}
\leq2^{-k/2}\leq\frac\alpha q, \tag{3}
\]
where the last inequality follows from \(k=\lceil8\log(2q/\alpha)\rceil\). A union bound over the fixed \(q\) coordinates proves simultaneous coverage once the calibrated \(K_\alpha\) in \(\widehat\rho_N\) is chosen at least as large as the fixed constant in (1)--(3), because deterministically
\[
\widehat\rho_N\geq K_\alpha\{1+M_{\mathrm{mom}}^{2/q_0}\}/\sqrt N.
\]

For completeness, the same median argument gives the required first moments rather than only a fixed tail probability. If \(r=\lceil k/2\rceil\), then for \(u\geq\Sigma/\sqrt{\min_b n_b}\),
\[
\Pr_P\{|\widehat\theta_j-\theta_j|>u\}
\leq2^k\left(\frac{\Sigma^2}{(\min_b n_b)u^2}\right)^r. \tag{4}
\]
Integrating (4), and using \(r>2\), yields
\[
\mathbb E_P|\widehat\theta_j-\theta_j|+\{\mathbb E_P|\widehat\theta_j-\theta_j|^2\}^{1/2}leq K_\alpha\Sigma N^{-1/2}. \tag{5}
\]

Let \(w_{bj}=n_b^{-1}\sum_{i\in b}(Z_{ij}-\widehat\theta_j)^2\). Since the median of nonnegative numbers is at most twice their average and the block sizes differ by at most one,
\[
\widehat v_j\leq \frac K N\sum_{i=1}^N(Z_{ij}-\widehat\theta_j)^2
\leq \frac{2K}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N(Z_{ij}-\theta_j)^2+2K(\widehat\theta_j-\theta_j)^2. \tag{6}
\]
Taking expectations in (6) and using (1) and (5) gives \(\sup_P\mathbb E_P\max_{j\leq q}\widehat v_j\leq K_\alpha\), because \(q\) is fixed. Jensen's inequality therefore gives \(\sup_P\mathbb E_P\widehat\rho_N\leq K_\alpha N^{-1/2}\). Summing (5) over coordinates gives \(\sup_P\mathbb E_P\|\widehat\theta-\theta(P)\|_{\mathsf m}\leq K_\alpha N^{-1/2}\). This proves both asserted bounds. Finally, by construction \(\mathsf F_N=\{N<2k_\alpha\}\) is false whenever \(N\geq2k_\alpha\), so its probability is exactly zero.

The unconditional upper inequality is exactly \(\operatorname{lem:pca-upper}\). For the lower inequality, apply \(\operatorname{lem:two-point-decision-lower-bounds}\) to the two laws in the displayed premise with \(\kappa=1/8\) and \(\Delta\geq c_0r_N\). Since \(\sqrt{\kappa/2}=1/4\), every estimator satisfies
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}\mathbb E_PL(\widetilde\mu,\mu(P))
\geq\frac38\min\{1,c_0^2r_N^2/4\}
\geq c r_N^2.
\]
Because \(r_N^2=\min\{1,(Ns_N^2)^{-1}\}\), taking the infimum over all measurable estimators proves the result.

Let \(\vartheta_0\) be the primitive parameter of a true \(P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)\). The conditional moment bound implies \(\|m_c\|\leq B\) and \(\sigma_c\leq B\), so \(\vartheta_0\in\overline\Theta_N(s_N)\). Direct evaluation of conditional first and second moments under the rank-two outcome equation, loading-error orthogonality, and spherical errors gives
\[
g(\vartheta_0)=\theta(P). \tag{1}
\]
Put \(E_N=\|\widehat\theta-\theta(P)\|_{\mathsf m}\). On the robust-ball event \(E_N\leq\widehat\rho_N\), the profiled distance satisfies \(d_N\leq E_N\), and hence
\[
\|g(\vartheta_0)-\widehat\theta\|_{\mathsf m}=E_N
\leq\widehat\rho_N\leq d_N+\widehat\rho_N.
\]
Thus \(\vartheta_0\in\mathcal C_N\), and the enclosing rectangle contains \(\mu(P)\). The coverage assertion in \(\operatorname{lem:robust-moment-ball}\) proves uniform level-\((1-\alpha)\) honesty for \(N\geq2k_\alpha\). For smaller \(N\), \(|\mu_{ct}|\leq B\) and the returned box \([-B,B]^{CT}\) covers with probability one.

For width, compactness of \(\overline\Theta_N(s_N)\) and continuity of \(g\) make the profiled minimum attainable and \(\mathcal C_N\) nonempty and compact. Its coordinate extrema are measurable: they are limits of extrema over deterministic finite \(1/j\)-nets after enlarging the continuous constraint by \(1/j\). For any \(\vartheta,\widetilde\vartheta\in\mathcal C_N\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|g(\vartheta)-g(\widetilde\vartheta)\|_{\mathsf m}
&\leq2(d_N+\widehat\rho_N)\\
&\leq2(E_N+\widehat\rho_N),
\end{aligned} \tag{2}
\]
where the last inequality uses the feasible true point in the definition of \(d_N\), without requiring the coverage event. Applying \(\operatorname{lem:observed-moment-inverse-modulus}\) to (2), the maximal target diameter of \(\mathcal C_N\) is at most
\[
K\min\!\left\{1,\frac{E_N+\widehat\rho_N}{s_N}\right\}. \tag{3}
\]
The enclosing rectangle has maximal half-width no larger than half this diameter. Since \(x\mapsto\min(1,x)\) is concave and increasing, \(\operatorname{lem:robust-moment-ball}\) and (3) give
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}\mathbb E_PW(\mathcal I_N)
\leq K\min\!\left\{1,\frac{\mathbb E_P(E_N+\widehat\rho_N)}{s_N}\right\}
\leq C_\alpha r_N. \tag{4}
\]
When \(N<2k_\alpha\), the width is bounded and \(r_N\geq(2k_\alpha)^{-1/2}\), so increasing \(C_\alpha\) proves (4) for all \(N\). The fallback event is deterministically empty once \(N\geq2k_\alpha\), proving the stated zero and little-oh assertions.

For the lower bound, apply \(\operatorname{lem:two-point-decision-lower-bounds}\) with \(\Delta\geq c_\alpha r_N\) and \(\kappa=(1-2\alpha)^2/8\). Then \(\sqrt{\kappa/2}=(1-2\alpha)/4\), and every honest rectangle has worst-case expected width at least
\[
\frac{3(1-2\alpha)}4\min\{1,c_\alpha r_N/2\}\geq c_\alpha' r_N.
\]
Taking the infimum over honest rectangles completes the proof.

If \(Ns_N^2\to\infty\), the unconditional upper bound in \(\operatorname{thm:minimax-frontier}\) converges to zero. Conversely, if \(Ns_N^2\) does not diverge, there are a finite \(M\) and a subsequence \(N_j\) with \(N_js_{N_j}^2\leq M\). Under the frontier-scale testing-pair premise, the lower bound in that theorem gives along this subsequence
\[
\inf_{\widetilde\mu}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{N_j}(s_{N_j})}\mathbb E_PL(\widetilde\mu,\mu(P))
\geq c\min\{1,M^{-1}\}>0.
\]
Thus convergence to zero is impossible, proving necessity. If \(s_N\geq s_0>0\), then for all large \(N\)
\[
\frac1N\leq\frac1{Ns_N^2}\leq\frac1{Ns_0^2},
\qquad
\frac1{\sqrt N}\leq\frac1{\sqrt N s_N}\leq\frac1{\sqrt N s_0}.
\]
The upper bounds in the two theorems therefore have orders \(N^{-1}\) and \(N^{-1/2}\); their lower bounds have the same orders under their respective testing-pair premises.

theorem.statement: The answer to \(\operatorname{oeq:four-mask-early-kill}\) is negative under the frozen assumptions. There are allowed fixed primitive radii and a legal equal-share four-mask family \((P_\eta)\), with \(s(P_\eta)\asymp|\eta|\) and every local factor restriction of rank two, for which \(\mu(P)=0\) for every law in the model. Hence no alternatives in the same shell can have \(\|\mu(P_{\eta,d})-\mu(P_{\eta,0})\|_\infty\geq c_1|d|\) for any \(c_1>0\) and \(d\ne0\), even though the shells are nonempty.
theorem.proof_tex:
Let \(q_0=4+\delta\), choose allowed constants \(v_\star=v^\star=v>0\) and \(M_{\mathrm{mom}}=(2v)^{q_0/2}\), and take \(p_c=1/4\) with \(p_\star<1/4\). For the four masks, let \(X_\eta\) have rows \((1,x_t)\), where
\[
(x_1,\ldots,x_6)=(1,2,3,4,5,19/5+\eta),
\]
and put \(\Gamma_\eta=X_\eta(X_\eta'X_\eta)^{-1/2}\). For sufficiently small \(|\eta|\), all four local restrictions have rank two. Compactness of a small closed \(\eta\)-neighborhood and continuity therefore permit a fixed
\[
0<g_\star<v\min_{c,\,|\eta|\leq\eta_0}\sigma_2(\Gamma_{\eta,S_c})^2.
\]
Conditional on every cohort, let \(\lambda_i\) be uniform on
\[
\{\sqrt{2v}e_1,-\sqrt{2v}e_1,\sqrt{2v}e_2,-\sqrt{2v}e_2\},
\]
and set \(\varepsilon_i=0\). Then \(m_c=0\), \(H_c=vI_2\), and
\[
\mathbb E\|\lambda_i\|^{q_0}=(2v)^{q_0/2}=M_{\mathrm{mom}}.
\]
Thus all rank, normalization, covariance, orthogonality, homoskedasticity, local-gap, and moment conditions hold. For nonzero sufficiently small \(\eta\), the relation rank is four, so these points are outside the mask relation-rank exceptional set. The proof of \(\operatorname{prop:o3-strict-inclusion}\) gives \(s(P_\eta)\asymp|\eta|>0\).

Choose any nonzero sequence \(\eta_N\to0\) and set \(s_N=s(P_{\eta_N})\). Since a padded projector relation is a contraction, \(s_N\leq1\), and \(P_{\eta_N}\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)\), so every shell is nonempty. But \(\operatorname{lem:tight-moment-radius-forces-zero-means}\) applies to every law in this model class, not only to the displayed family, and gives \(\mu(P)=0\). Therefore the requested positive target separation is impossible for every pair of same-shell laws. This falsifies the conjunction in the open-ended question.

theorem.statement: The answer to \(\operatorname{oeq:shell-deformation}\) is negative: nonemptiness of \(\mathcal P_N(s_N)\) does not imply any positive target-separating deformation under the frozen primitive restrictions. In particular, there are allowed fixed primitive radii and a sequence of nonempty four-mask shells for which \(\mu(P)=0\) for every \(P\) in the ambient model, so the requested order-\(|d|\) separation fails for every \(d\ne0\). Moreover, the original condition \(0<|d|\leq c_0\min\{1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}\) has no lower bound on \(|d|\) and therefore, even when pairs exist, does not by itself imply a frontier-scale minimax lower bound.
theorem.proof_tex:
Use exactly the legal family and fixed radii constructed in the proof of \(\operatorname{thm:four-mask-early-kill-negative}\), and set \(s_N=s(P_{\eta_N})\) for a nonzero sequence \(\eta_N\to0\). Then \(P_{\eta_N}\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)\), so the shells are nonempty. By \(\operatorname{lem:tight-moment-radius-forces-zero-means}\), every \(P\in\mathcal M\), hence every \(P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)\), satisfies \(\mu(P)=0\). Thus for any two same-shell laws
\[
\|\mu(P_d)-\mu(P_0)\|_\infty=0,
\]
which contradicts the requested lower bound \(c_1|d|>0\). This is an explicit nonempty-shell counterexample. Separately, the displayed upper restriction on \(|d|\) permits a sequence \(|d|=o\{\min(1,(\sqrt Ns_N)^{-1})\}\); squaring such a separation cannot yield a constant multiple of \(\min\{1,(Ns_N^2)^{-1}\}\). Hence a lower scale (and testing-valid divergence) must be part of any premise used for the frontier.

added_lemmas.statement: Let \(q_0=4+\delta\). If the allowed primitive constants obey \(v_{\star}=v^{\star}=v>0\) and \(M_{\mathrm{mom}}=(2v)^{q_0/2}\), then every \(P\in\mathcal M\) has \(m_c=0\) and \(\varepsilon_i=0\) almost surely conditional on \(C_i=c\), for every \(c\). In particular, \(\mu(P)=0\) throughout this allowed model class.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(c\) and put \(q_0=4+\delta>2\). The two covariance bounds with equal endpoints give
\[
H_c=vI_2.
\]
By the conditional moment-radius assumption, Lyapunov's inequality, and the identity \(\mathbb E_P\|\lambda_i\|^2\mid C_i=c=\operatorname{tr}(H_c)+\|m_c\|^2\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
(2v)^{q_0/2}=M_{\mathrm{mom}}
&\geq \mathbb E_P\!\left[\|\lambda_i\|^{q_0}+\|\varepsilon_i\|^{q_0}\mid C_i=c\right]\\
&\geq \mathbb E_P[\|\lambda_i\|^{q_0}\mid C_i=c]\\
&\geq \left\{\mathbb E_P[\|\lambda_i\|^2\mid C_i=c]\right\}^{q_0/2}\\
&=(2v+\|m_c\|^2)^{q_0/2}\geq(2v)^{q_0/2}.
\end{aligned}
\]
All inequalities are therefore equalities. Strict monotonicity of \(x\mapsto x^{q_0/2}\) gives \(m_c=0\), and equality in the first line gives \(\mathbb E_P[\|\varepsilon_i\|^{q_0}\mid C_i=c]=0\), hence \(\varepsilon_i=0\) almost surely conditional on the cohort. Finally the rank-two outcome equation and the conditional error-mean restriction give \(\mu_c(P)=\Gamma m_c=0\). The argument applies to every cohort.

added_lemmas.statement:
There is a constant \(K\), depending only on the fixed primitive radii and \((T,C)\), such that for every \(N\), every \(s_N\in(0,1]\), and every \(\vartheta,\widetilde\vartheta\in\overline\Theta_N(s_N)\),
\[
\max_{c\in[C]}\|\Gamma m_c-\widetilde\Gamma\widetilde m_c\|_\infty
\leq K\min\!\left\{1,\frac{\|g(\vartheta)-g(\widetilde\vartheta)\|_{\mathsf m}}{s_N}\right\}.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(e=\|g(\vartheta)-g(\widetilde\vartheta)\|_{\mathsf m}\). All norms below are equivalent with constants depending only on fixed \((T,C)\). The first coordinates of \(g\) imply \(|p_c-\widetilde p_c|\leq e\). Since \(p_c,\widetilde p_c\geq p_\star\), division by cohort shares is valid. The loading-mean moment restriction gives \(\|m_c\|,\|\widetilde m_c\|\leq B\), while \(H_c,\widetilde H_c\preceq v^\star I_2\), \(\sigma_c,\widetilde\sigma_c\leq B\), and \(\|\Gamma\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\|\widetilde\Gamma\|_{\mathrm{op}}=1\). Hence the conditional first and second raw moments are uniformly bounded. Dividing the corresponding weighted coordinates of \(g\) by \(p_c\) and \(\widetilde p_c\), and then subtracting the outer products of the conditional means, yields
\[
\max_c\{\|\nu_c-\widetilde\nu_c\|+\|V_c-\widetilde V_c\|_{\mathrm F}\}\leq K e. \tag{1}
\]

Let \(P_c=I-Q_c\) and \(\widetilde P_c=I-\widetilde Q_c\). The two signal eigenvalues of \(V_c\) exceed its remaining eigenvalue \(\sigma_c^2\) by at least \(g_\star\). Thus for every rank-two projector \(P\), spectral decomposition gives
\[
\operatorname{tr}\{V_c(P_c-P)\}\geq \frac{g_\star}{2}\|P_c-P\|_{\mathrm F}^2. \tag{2}
\]
Because \(\widetilde P_c\) maximizes \(P\mapsto\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde V_cP)\) over rank-two projectors,
\[
\operatorname{tr}\{V_c(P_c-\widetilde P_c)\}
\leq \operatorname{tr}\{(V_c-\widetilde V_c)(P_c-\widetilde P_c)\}
\leq \|V_c-\widetilde V_c\|_{\mathrm F}\|P_c-\widetilde P_c\|_{\mathrm F}.
\]
Combining this display with (1)--(2) proves \(\max_c\|Q_c-\widetilde Q_c\|_{\mathrm F}\leq Ke\).

Use the padded relation matrices
\[
\mathcal R=\operatorname{stack}_{c=1}^C\sqrt{p_c}\,Q_cJ_c,
\qquad
\widetilde{\mathcal R}=\operatorname{stack}_{c=1}^C\sqrt{\widetilde p_c}\,\widetilde Q_cJ_c.
\]
They have Gram matrices \(A(P)\) and \(A(\widetilde P)\), respectively, and therefore have the same singular values and kernels as the relation constructions in the core. Since \(p_c,\widetilde p_c\geq p_\star\), (1) and the preceding projector bound imply
\[
\|\mathcal R-\widetilde{\mathcal R}\|_{\mathrm F}\leq Ke. \tag{3}
\]
Let \(U,\widetilde U\) be orthonormal bases for their two-dimensional kernels. For every matrix \(X\) with columns orthogonal to \(U\), the margin restriction gives \(\|\mathcal RX\|_{\mathrm F}\geq s_N\|X\|_{\mathrm F}\). Since \(\widetilde{\mathcal R}\widetilde U=0\), (3) gives
\[
s_N\|(I-UU')\widetilde U\|_{\mathrm F}
\leq \|\mathcal R\widetilde U\|_{\mathrm F}
\leq \|\mathcal R-\widetilde{\mathcal R}\|_{\mathrm F}\|\widetilde U\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\leq Ke. \tag{4}
\]

The local signal-gap and loading upper bound imply
\[
g_\star\leq\lambda_2(\Gamma_{S_c}H_c\Gamma_{S_c}')
\leq v^\star\sigma_2(\Gamma_{S_c})^2,
\qquad
\sigma_2(\Gamma_{S_c})\geq a:=\sqrt{g_\star/v^\star}>0. \tag{5}
\]
The same bound holds for \(\widetilde\Gamma_{S_c}\). If the right side of (4) is at most a sufficiently small fixed constant, an orthogonal change of basis aligns \(\widetilde U\) to \(U\) with \(\|U-\widetilde U\|_{\mathrm F}\leq K e/s_N\). Formula (5), the identity
\[
G^{-1}-\widetilde G^{-1}=G^{-1}(\widetilde G-G)\widetilde G^{-1},
\]
and direct multiplication then show that the reconstruction maps
\[
K_c(U)=U(U_{S_c}'U_{S_c})^{-1}U_{S_c}'
\]
satisfy \(\|K_c(U)-K_c(\widetilde U)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq Ke/s_N\). Since \(\nu_c=U_{S_c}r_c\) for some \(r_c\), the core functional gives \(K_c(U)\nu_c=\Gamma m_c\), and similarly for the tilded parameter. Therefore (1) implies
\[
\|\Gamma m_c-\widetilde\Gamma\widetilde m_c\|_\infty
\leq K\{e+e/s_N\}\leq Ke/s_N.
\]
If the smallness condition fails, both target vectors have coordinates bounded by \(B\), so the left side is at most \(2B\), which is bounded by a fixed multiple of \(\min\{1,e/s_N\}\) in that regime. This proves the global assertion.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(P_0^N,P_1^N\) be two observed-sample laws, put \(\Delta=\|\mu(P_1)-\mu(P_0)\|_\infty\), and suppose \(\operatorname{KL}(P_0^N,P_1^N)\leq\kappa<\infty\). Then every estimator \(\widetilde\mu\) satisfies
\[
\max_{j\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E_{P_j}L(\widetilde\mu,\mu(P_j))
\geq \frac{1-\sqrt{\kappa/2}}{2}\min\{1,\Delta^2/4\}.
\]
Moreover, every rectangle honest at both laws satisfies
\[
\max_{j\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E_{P_j}W(\mathcal I_N)
\geq \bigl(1-2\alpha-\sqrt{\kappa/2}\bigr)_+\min\{1,\Delta/2\}.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
First we derive the probability-distance bound used below. For an event \(E\), put \(p=P_0^N(E)\) and \(q=P_1^N(E)\). Conditioning the likelihood ratio on \(E\) and \(E^c\), and applying Jensen's inequality on each cell, gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_0^N,P_1^N)\geq p\log\frac pq+(1-p)\log\frac{1-p}{1-q}=:k(p,q).
\]
For fixed \(q\in(0,1)\), the function \(f(p)=k(p,q)-2(p-q)^2\) has \(f(q)=f'(q)=0\) and
\[
f''(p)=\frac1p+\frac1{1-p}-4=\frac1{p(1-p)}-4\geq0.
\]
The boundary cases follow by limits. Thus \(k(p,q)\geq2(p-q)^2\); taking the supremum over events proves
\[
\operatorname{TV}(P_0^N,P_1^N)\leq\sqrt{\kappa/2}. \tag{1}
\]

Choose a coordinate \((c,t)\) attaining \(\Delta\), and define a test that selects the parameter value closer to \(\widetilde\mu_{ct}\). Whenever this test errs under \(P_j^N\), the triangle inequality gives \(|\widetilde\mu_{ct}-\mu_{ct}(P_j)|\geq\Delta/2\), and hence the loss is at least \(\min\{1,\Delta^2/4\}\). The sum of the two testing-error probabilities is at least \(1-\operatorname{TV}(P_0^N,P_1^N)\). Averaging the two risks and applying (1) proves the first assertion.

For the rectangle claim, under \(P_0^N\) the event that the rectangle covers \(\mu(P_0)\) has probability at least \(1-\alpha\). Honesty under \(P_1^N\) and (1) imply that, under \(P_0^N\), the event that it covers \(\mu(P_1)\) has probability at least \(1-\alpha-\sqrt{\kappa/2}\). Their intersection therefore has probability at least \(1-2\alpha-\sqrt{\kappa/2}\). On the intersection, the interval in coordinate \((c,t)\) contains two points separated by \(\Delta\), so its half-width is at least \(\Delta/2\). The definition of \(W\) completes the proof.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Define acceptance by the rank-two Lei--Ross \(O_3\) procedure to mean convergence to one super-cohort whose observed-outcome union is \([T]\). Under the canonical anchor encoding, such acceptance implies \(r_{1,2}(H_3)=T-2\). The implication is strict: for \(T=6\) and masks \(123,145,256,346\), \(O_3\) has no edge whereas \(r_{1,2}(H_3)=4=T-2\). For the raw rows in \(\operatorname{def:four-mask-witness}\), \(D\Gamma_{\mathrm{raw}}=0\), \(\operatorname{rank}(D)=4\), and the first-four-column minor is \(-11\). With equal shares and unit-normalized relation rows at sixth slope \(z=6\), \(0.16936528<s<0.16936530\). If instead \(z=19/5+\eta\), with equal shares and the factor plane obtained by orthonormalizing the rows \((1,t)\), then \(s(P_\eta)\asymp|\eta|\) for sufficiently small \(|\eta|\), and every local matrix \(\Gamma_{S_c}\) has rank two.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original decimal asserted an exact equality although it was a rounded numerical value, and neither O3 acceptance nor the law along the slope path specified outcome coverage, equal shares, or orthonormalization. The replacement states a certified rational interval and makes those necessary conventions explicit.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Put \(r_N=\min\{1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}\). For every sequence of nonempty shells for which there exist \(P_{N,0},P_{N,1}\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)\) and a constant \(c_0>0\), uniform in \(N\), such that
\[
\|\mu(P_{N,1})-\mu(P_{N,0})\|_\infty\geq c_0r_N,
\qquad
\operatorname{KL}(P_{N,0,O}^N,P_{N,1,O}^N)\leq1/8,
\]
one has
\[
c\min\{1,(Ns_N^2)^{-1}\}
\leq\inf_{\widetilde\mu}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}\mathbb E_PL(\widetilde\mu,\mu(P))
\leq C_0\min\{1,(Ns_N^2)^{-1}\}.
\]
The infimum ranges over every measurable estimator of the entire observed sample. For every nonempty shell, without the displayed testing-pair premise, only the upper inequality is asserted and is attained by the corrected estimator in \(\operatorname{def:pca-estimator}\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original deformation question requires only 0<|d| at most the frontier scale. It permits arbitrarily smaller separations and places no testing-valid numerical upper bound on divergence, so it cannot imply the claimed rate. The replacement restricts the lower-bound regime to explicit frontier-scale pairs with KL at most 1/8; the upper bound remains unconditional.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Put \(r_N=\min\{1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}\). For every sequence of nonempty shells for which there exist \(P_{N,0},P_{N,1}\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)\) and \(c_\alpha>0\), uniform in \(N\), such that
\[
\|\mu(P_{N,1})-\mu(P_{N,0})\|_\infty\geq c_\alpha r_N,
\qquad
\operatorname{KL}(P_{N,0,O}^N,P_{N,1,O}^N)\leq(1-2\alpha)^2/8,
\]
one has
\[
c_\alpha' r_N
\leq\inf_{\mathcal I_N\in\mathfrak I_{N,\alpha}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}\mathbb E_PW(\mathcal I_N)
\leq C_\alpha r_N.
\]
For every nonempty shell, without the displayed testing-pair premise, the profile-recentered inversion in \(\operatorname{def:moment-inversion}\) is uniformly level-\((1-\alpha)\) honest and attains the upper inequality. Its full-box fallback occurs only on \(\mathsf F_N=\{N<2k_\alpha\}\), so for all sufficiently large \(N\) its expected fallback contribution is zero and hence \(o\{(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}\), uniformly because \(s_N\leq1\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: A positive honest-width lower bound requires both frontier-scale target separation and total variation strictly below 1-2alpha. The original deformation question supplies neither a lower scale for |d| nor an alpha-calibrated divergence bound. The replacement makes exactly those testing conditions explicit and retains the unconditional inversion upper bound.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
On every sequence of nonempty shells satisfying the frontier-scale testing-pair premise in \(\operatorname{thm:minimax-frontier}\),
\[
\inf_{\widetilde\mu}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}\mathbb E_PL(\widetilde\mu,\mu(P))\longrightarrow0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
Ns_N^2\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Without that premise, \(Ns_N^2\to\infty\) remains sufficient. In the regular special case \(s_N\geq s_0>0\), the available upper scales are \(N^{-1}\) for squared risk and \(N^{-1/2}\) for honest maximal half-width; the matching lower scales hold under the corresponding testing-pair premises in \(\operatorname{thm:minimax-frontier}\) and \(\operatorname{thm:honest-rectangle}\).

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Estimate \(\nu_c\) and \(V_c\) by cohort sample moments, form \(\widehat Q_c=I-\Pi_2(\widehat V_c)\) and \(\widehat A=\sum_c\widehat p_cJ_c^{\prime}\widehat Q_cJ_c\), and take \(\widehat U\) as its bottom two eigenvectors, using fixed deterministic Borel tie-breaking conventions for every eigenspace and basis. Whenever all required cohort moments and inverses exist, set
\[
\widehat\mu_c=\operatorname{clip}_{[-B,B]^T}\!\left\{\widehat U(\widehat U_{S_c}^{\prime}\widehat U_{S_c})^{-1}\widehat U_{S_c}^{\prime}\widehat\nu_c\right\}.
\]
If a required cohort moment is unavailable or any displayed inverse does not exist, set the entire vector \(\widehat\mu\) equal to zero. Thus the construction is everywhere a measurable element of \(\mathbb R^{C\times T}\).
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The existing fallback says a vector-valued estimator uses a full box, which is ill typed. The corrected construction returns the zero vector on unavailable-moment or singular-inverse branches while retaining the clipped PCA formula otherwise.

proposed.statement: Define acceptance by the rank-two Lei--Ross \(O_3\) procedure to mean convergence to one super-cohort whose observed-outcome union is \([T]\). Under the canonical anchor encoding, such acceptance implies \(r_{1,2}(H_3)=T-2\). The implication is strict: for \(T=6\) and masks \(123,145,256,346\), \(O_3\) has no edge whereas \(r_{1,2}(H_3)=4=T-2\). For the raw rows in \(\operatorname{def:four-mask-witness}\), \(D\Gamma_{\mathrm{raw}}=0\), \(\operatorname{rank}(D)=4\), and the first-four-column minor is \(-11\). With equal shares and unit-normalized relation rows at sixth slope \(z=6\), \(0.16936528<s<0.16936530\). If instead \(z=19/5+\eta\), with equal shares and the factor plane obtained by orthonormalizing the rows \((1,t)\), then \(s(P_\eta)\asymp|\eta|\) for sufficiently small \(|\eta|\), and every local matrix \(\Gamma_{S_c}\) has rank two.
proposed.justification: This panel-specific corollary locates the published \(O_3\) screen inside the published count acceptance region and records an exact strict witness and singular path; it is not a new generic sparsity theorem.
proposed.gap: Lei and Ross prove \(O_3\) sufficiency, while the deterministic count criterion is due to Pimentel-Alarcón, Boston, and Nowak; the panel-specific delta is the explicit containment check and strict causal-panel mask witness.
proposed.consumer: The strict witness is a regression test for mask screening in \(\operatorname{apm}\) and \(\operatorname{fect}\) workflows and supplies the early-kill path for singular-shell analysis.

proposed.statement:
Put \(r_N=\min\{1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}\). For every sequence of nonempty shells for which there exist \(P_{N,0},P_{N,1}\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)\) and a constant \(c_0>0\), uniform in \(N\), such that
\[
\|\mu(P_{N,1})-\mu(P_{N,0})\|_\infty\geq c_0r_N,
\qquad
\operatorname{KL}(P_{N,0,O}^N,P_{N,1,O}^N)\leq1/8,
\]
one has
\[
c\min\{1,(Ns_N^2)^{-1}\}
\leq\inf_{\widetilde\mu}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}\mathbb E_PL(\widetilde\mu,\mu(P))
\leq C_0\min\{1,(Ns_N^2)^{-1}\}.
\]
The infimum ranges over every measurable estimator of the entire observed sample. For every nonempty shell, without the displayed testing-pair premise, only the upper inequality is asserted and is attained by the corrected estimator in \(\operatorname{def:pca-estimator}\).
proposed.justification: Conditional on a visible testing-valid same-shell pair at the frontier scale, the matched frontier turns the APM eigenvalue into the exact information scale; achievability remains unconditional on nonempty shells.
proposed.gap: Lei and Ross require the APM gap to dominate estimation noise, and Yan and Wainwright study a different growing-matrix experiment; conditional on legal frontier-scale same-shell pairs, this theorem supplies the fixed-panel complete-law converse against the same observable-shell upper bound.
proposed.consumer: Researchers using \(\operatorname{apm}\) or \(\operatorname{fect}\) obtain the sharp recovery rate whenever the explicit testing-pair certificate is available.

proposed.statement: The estimator in \(\operatorname{def:pca-estimator}\) satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}\mathbb E_P L(\widehat\mu,\mu(P))\le K\min\{1,(Ns_N^2)^{-1}\}\), where \(K\) depends only on the fixed primitive radii and \((T,C)\).
proposed.justification: A finite-sample risk bound is the achievability half needed to distinguish genuine statistical weakness from a fragile proof of consistency.
proposed.gap: Lei and Ross give fixed-point asymptotic linearity, while Srivastava and Pimentel-Alarcón give a projection perturbation bound; neither supplies the causal mean risk bound uniformly over shrinking shells with cohort moments estimated from the full sample.
proposed.consumer: The bound supplies a tuning-free error scale for rank-two counterfactual means returned by covariance-PCA implementations.

proposed.statement:
Put \(r_N=\min\{1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}\). For every sequence of nonempty shells for which there exist \(P_{N,0},P_{N,1}\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)\) and \(c_\alpha>0\), uniform in \(N\), such that
\[
\|\mu(P_{N,1})-\mu(P_{N,0})\|_\infty\geq c_\alpha r_N,
\qquad
\operatorname{KL}(P_{N,0,O}^N,P_{N,1,O}^N)\leq(1-2\alpha)^2/8,
\]
one has
\[
c_\alpha' r_N
\leq\inf_{\mathcal I_N\in\mathfrak I_{N,\alpha}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}\mathbb E_PW(\mathcal I_N)
\leq C_\alpha r_N.
\]
For every nonempty shell, without the displayed testing-pair premise, the profile-recentered inversion in \(\operatorname{def:moment-inversion}\) is uniformly level-\((1-\alpha)\) honest and attains the upper inequality. Its full-box fallback occurs only on \(\mathsf F_N=\{N<2k_\alpha\}\), so for all sufficiently large \(N\) its expected fallback contribution is zero and hence \(o\{(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}\), uniformly because \(s_N\leq1\).
proposed.justification: Profile recentering makes the nonlinear feasible set nonempty, a calibrated data-driven moment radius gives uniform coverage, and a testing-valid same-shell pair gives the lower width.
proposed.gap: Andrews and Cheng establish generic identification-robust inversion, and Zhu establishes weak-factor honesty costs; neither provides this total finite-moment inversion rule or the panel-specific observed-moment inverse modulus.
proposed.consumer: The result provides simultaneous uncertainty bands for all missing untreated means in the Veneto wage application and in interactive-fixed-effect event studies without relying on pointwise Wald linearization.
